# Email Sift Rubric

Sift labels new Gmail by importance on a schedule, and reads this doc in full before every run. It's my definition of what matters. Every rule above "Added by sift" is mine, and sift never changes those. Keep it under about two pages.

Timezone: America/Chicago

## How to use this doc

- **Change a rule:** edit any section above "Added by sift". Sift never changes those.
- **Correct a label:** in Gmail, swap the AI label for the right one, or add Wrong. Sift learns from it on its next run and records the change in the Changelog.
- **Answer a question:** sift asks in comments that start with "Sift:". Reply in the thread, and the next run applies your answer.
- **Choose newsletters:** list the ones I want to read under Newsletters, Valued. Every other newsletter gets Bulk. Sift adds lines there too, each starting with "(learned)", when I correct a newsletter's label.
- **Allow more than labels:** add it under Permissions, for example "Archive threads labeled Junk".
- **Tell sift about yourself:** add notes under About me, grouped by topic. Sift adds its own notes there too, each starting with "(inferred)". Edit one to correct it, or remove "(inferred)" to make it yours.

## Labels

| Label | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Important | I'd want to see it today |
| Low priority | Meant for me, nothing urgent |
| Bulk | Mass mail I wouldn't miss if it were archived unread |
| Junk | Mail I never want |
| Needs reply | Someone is waiting on me |
| Sifted | Sift has evaluated it |
| Wrong | I add this to flag a bad call |
| Soccer | My own label; sift doesn't apply it |
| Receipts | My own label; sift doesn't apply it |
| School | My own label; sift doesn't apply it |

## About me

Who I am, the people in my mail, and what matters to me right now, grouped by topic so related notes sit together. Sift reads this before every run. Lines I write are mine. Sift adds lines that start with "(inferred)", with where it learned each one and when, and it edits only those lines. To keep related notes together, sift may move any line here, mine included, but never changes my words.

### (topic, such as Kids' soccer, Home, or Work)

- (I add these)

## Always important

Senders, topics, or situations that should always get Important.

- Anything from a person I have written to in the last 90 days, unless it is clearly bulk mail
- Deadlines, payments, or schedule changes affecting the next 7 days
- Anything from my kids' coaches or teachers

## Needs reply

What counts as someone waiting on me specifically. It depends on the message, not on who sent it.

- A direct question addressed to me by name or as the only recipient
- Requests for a decision, approval, or volunteer sign-up
- A statement addressed to me that needs me to acknowledge it, such as a confirmation someone is waiting on

Not a reply, even from someone I know:

- A message to a group that only shares information, such as a note to all tenants about a visit
- An acknowledgment of my own message, such as "ok, thanks" or "got it"

## Low priority

Mail meant for me that doesn't meet the rules above, including:

- Automated notifications that only confirm something already done
- Group threads where I am Cc'd and nothing is asked of me
- Newsletters on my Valued list
- Receipts and statements
- FYIs from people I know

## Bulk

Mass mail I wouldn't miss if it were archived unread, including:

- Newsletters not on my Valued list
- Promotions from companies I've signed up with or bought from
- Social network notifications

## Newsletters

Valued newsletters get Low priority. Every other newsletter, listed under Not valued or not listed at all, gets Bulk. One per line: name | sender.

### Valued

- (I add these)

### Not valued

- (I add these)

## Junk

Mail I never want, including:

- Promotions and marketing I didn't ask for, even when worded urgently
- Spam-like or phishing-like messages

## Category labels

Labels sift adds alongside the priority label, judged on what a message is, not on the words it happens to use. Sift creates each one by name.

- **Receipts, statements, and invoices:** label a message Receipt, Statement, or Invoice when it is one, or carries one as an attachment. A message that only talks about one, such as "where is my receipt for Thursday?" or "I never got an invoice in the mail", gets none of these labels.
- **Newsletters:** label a message Newsletter when it works as a newsletter, whatever it calls itself: a "newsletter", a "gazette", or a regular Friday update that reads like one.
- **Travel:** label Travel the booking confirmations, itineraries, boarding passes, and check-in reminders for trips I've booked. Travel deals and "where to next?" marketing don't count.
- **Deliveries:** label Delivery the tracking updates, "out for delivery", and "delivered" notices for orders I've placed. Shipping promotions don't count.
- **Appointments:** label Appointment the confirmations, reminders, and reschedules for appointments I have, such as a doctor, dentist, or car service. "Book your next visit" promotions don't count.
- **Account security:** label Security the sign-in alerts, password resets, and verification codes from services I use. A message that only looks like one, from a lookalike sender, is Junk instead.

## Added by sift

Rules sift learned from my corrections. Sift adds, sharpens, and consolidates rules only here. A rule here can narrow one of mine for the cases it names.

- Automated notices from orders@bookshop.example are Low priority
- Price-change notices from billing@streamflix.example are Bulk

## Permissions

Actions beyond priority labels that sift may take, by category. Empty means priority labels only. For example: "Archive threads labeled Junk", or "Label event invitations as invitation". Sift creates any label I name here in title case (Invitation), or uses mine when I already have one by that name.

Real cases that teach the rules. Format: sender | subject | correct label | why.

Newest first. Date | change | prompted by.
